$comment: The shared contract: what a webhook has to carry to be accepted, and every way one is refused.
A change here is a change to every SDK. Each target reads this file from its own suite and runs
every vector through its own verification, so a vector added here is exercised by every target
without any of them being edited, and a target that accepts what the others refuse fails.
The codes were computed outside every implementation, with a general-purpose HMAC tool. A suite
that signed with the module it is testing and verified with the same module would pass whatever
the two agreed on; these hold each implementation against an answer it had no say in.
A vector is self-contained: the secret, the body, the headers as delivered, the signature header,
the moment to hold it against and the tolerance to hold it within. `verdict` is `accepted` or
`refused`; a refused one names which of `refusals` it is refused as, so a client that refuses
the right vector for the wrong reason — computing a code over a header that never arrived, and
reporting a mismatch — fails as well. A target maps those names onto its own failures.
The message a code is computed over is the moment, then `.`, then for the header scheme the
covered names joined by a space, `.`, their values in that same order joined by `.`, `.`, and
then the body; the body scheme is the moment, `.`, and the body.

vectors.name: a body-scheme signature verifies
vectors.reason: the older scheme covers the moment and the body, which is what this code was computed over

vectors.name: a header-scheme signature verifies
vectors.reason: the newer scheme also covers the headers it names, and their values arrived as signed

vectors.name: the header scheme is the one verified when both are offered
vectors.reason: the stronger code is the right one, and the weaker one beside it is never looked at

vectors.name: a right weaker code does not rescue a wrong stronger one
vectors.reason: accepting the weaker of two schemes because the sender also offered it is how a downgrade works

vectors.name: the order the covered headers are named in is part of what is signed
vectors.reason: the same two headers named the other way round cover their values the other way round, which is a different message

vectors.name: the covered headers are read in the order the signature names them
vectors.reason: the same two headers, signed in the order this signature names them, verify

vectors.name: a header the signature covers that the request did not carry
vectors.reason: signing over an absent value would let a sender drop a header and keep the signature valid, so it is refused before any code is computed

vectors.name: a code that is not hexadecimal
vectors.reason: a decoder that stops at the first character it cannot read compares a prefix, and a prefix of the right code is not the right code

vectors.name: a code that is not whole
vectors.reason: half a byte is missing from the code, and reading the rest of it would compare something shorter than what was signed

vectors.name: a moment older than the tolerance
vectors.reason: the code is the right one for that moment, and the moment is one second past the window, which is what bounds how long a captured delivery can be replayed

vectors.name: a moment further ahead than the tolerance
vectors.reason: a window that only looks backwards is one a sender widens by dating its own delivery in the future

vectors.name: a moment at the edge of the window
vectors.reason: the tolerance is the width a delivery is accepted within, so its own edge is inside it
